items.q: What brain circuits does Huberman map meditation onto?
items.a: Meditation is **goal-specific neuroplasticity**, not one practice. The triad is **left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex** (interpreter/decision), **ACC** (bodily signal integration), and **insula** (matching internal + external context). You place up to **~2 perceptual spotlights** along the **interoception–exteroception continuum**.

items.q: Why does closing your eyes change the practice so much?
items.a: Eyes closed shut a major exteroceptive channel — **~40% of cortex is visual** — so **ACC + insula ramp up** toward interoception. The classic *"third eye"* is the **prefrontal cortex, not the pineal**; with **no sensation there**, thoughts and memories geyser up.

items.q: How do you choose the right meditation for today's state?
items.a: Use the **meditation challenge principle**: check your momentary **interoceptive vs exteroceptive bias** (eyes closed vs open). **Do the opposite of your default** — friction signals plasticity; *"if something were easy… there is absolutely zero reason for your neural circuits to change."*

items.q: What skill are expert meditators actually training?
items.a: They **refocus faster**, not hold focus longer. Every **mind-wander + return** is a training rep — *"the more number of times you have to refocus, the better training you're getting."*

items.q: How should breath set your exit state?
items.a: **Longer/vigorous inhales → alertness**; **longer/vigorous exhales → calm**. Complex or non-cyclic patterns (box, double-inhale) force **interoception**. Decide before the session: do you need **calm or alert** when you leave?

items.q: Why does mind-wandering matter for happiness?
items.a: Killingsworth & Gilbert (*Science* 2010): a **wandering mind is an unhappy mind** — mind-wandering predicts unhappiness **more than the activity itself**. Presence can feel better even during **unpleasant tasks**.

items.q: Should you do focus meditation before bed?
items.a: Traditional **third-eye/focus meditation can impair sleep** near bedtime (Wendy Suzuki **13-min** study). For restoration use **yoga nidra / NSDR** — anti-focus body scans that can **lower cortisol** and **replenish dopamine**.

items.q: What dose and consistency rules does Huberman cite?
items.a: **~3 minutes** can be a minimum effective dose; the **daily 13 min × 8 weeks** protocol is a memory/mood benchmark. **Consistency beats duration** — weekly **30 min** can beat daily **3 min** if that's what you'll actually do. Better meditators need **less time** for trait benefits (*Altered Traits*).

items.q: How is clinical hypnosis different from meditation?
items.a: **Hypnosis ≠ meditation**: clinical hypnosis (e.g. Reveri/Spiegel) targets **specific problems**; meditation and NSDR are **general state tools**. Also match practice to the **interoception–dissociation continuum** — too inward (anxiety hyper-awareness) vs too dissociated — healthy sits in a **U-shaped trench**.
